messages:
nora: hi team, nora here (first day!). following the onboarding guide but my kubeconfig doesn't include the redwood-dev context and I can't access my team namespace. who handles RBAC/namespace setup?
kai-infra: welcome! pinging infra. quick check: did you run the cloud login step? (aws sso login --profile redwood or gcloud auth login). also paste `kubectl config get-contexts` if you can.
nora: pasted:
CURRENT   NAME               CLUSTER        AUTHINFO
          local              local-cluster  local-user
*         ci                 ci-cluster     ci-sa
no redwood-dev showing. I did the aws step but maybe I missed the eks update command.
onboard-bot: ticket ONB-442 created for nora: "request namespace RoleBinding and kubecontext alias". Assigned to kai-infra.
kai-infra: run `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --alias redwood-dev` then `kubectl config get-contexts`. If you still get forbidden errors when listing pods in `team-nora`, reply here and I'll create a RoleBinding.
nora: ran update-kubeconfig, now context present. switched to it but `kubectl get pods -n team-nora` -> Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden.
kai-infra: okay you're not in the `redwood-developers` group yet. I'll create a RoleBinding rb-nora-onboard binding your SSO email to the edit role for namespace `team-nora` for first-week access. Confirm your SSO email?
nora: nora@redwood.ai
kai-infra: done  I created RoleBinding `rb-nora-onboard`. Wait ~20s and try `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n team-nora`. Also if you see token errors run `aws sso login` again then `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev`.
maya-sec: heads-up on secrets: we grant `secrets-get` for short-lived dev access only. Open a secrets ticket with justification if you need it, and include the TTL you need. We'll review.
nora: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n team-nora` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n team-nora` -> No resources found. good. set default namespace with `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=team-nora` so no need for -n.
ryan-eng: welcome! small note: if your kubeconfig merged duplicate user entries from previous clusters you might get confusing "Unauthorized" messages. clean by exporting minified config: `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > ~/.kube/config` then re-run aws sso login. saved me earlier.
nora: thanks everyone, working now and added the onboarding checklist item about running `aws eks update-kubeconfig`. appreciate the fast help :smile:
